Texture School

KITCHEN NOTES / PREPARE BETTER

Keep your salad crisp

A little less water. A lot more crunch. Give the ingredients a moment before the dressing goes in.

Drain → Dry → Dress
Go to the technique ↓

THE SMALL DETAILS THAT HELP

Here's how.

  1. 01

    Drain the chickpeas

    Tip cooked canned chickpeas into a sieve, rinse, then let the water run off.

    Look for Look underneath: the stream should have slowed to occasional drips.

  2. 02

    Dry the surfaces

    Pat the chickpeas gently with a clean towel. Dry washed cucumber and herbs before chopping.

    Look for Surface water should not collect in the bottom of your mixing bowl.

  3. 03

    Keep the pieces chunky

    Cut cucumber into bite-size pieces. If the seed centre is very watery, scoop some out first.

    Look for Aim for pieces that hold their shape when you toss them.

  4. 04

    Dress when ready to serve

    Add a little dressing, toss gently, then decide whether the salad needs more.

    Look for The ingredients should look lightly coated, with no large puddle underneath.

A note worth keeping

Know what to look for.

Lift a spoonful: the dressing clings lightly and the cucumber still looks firm.

Try it in a recipe ↓

AVOID THIS

Pouring dressing onto ingredients that are still dripping.

Extra water dilutes the dressing and collects at the bottom of the bowl.

TRY THIS INSTEAD

Drain and dry first. Add the dressing gradually.

MAKE SUBSTITUTIONS

Keep the job. Expect a change.

Out of chickpeas? Cooked white beans can take their place, but fold them in gently because they can be softer. This is a texture change, not an identical result.

Already a little watery?

Lift the salad into a clean bowl with a slotted spoon. Taste before adding more dressing; adding extra oil alone will not remove the water.
